teaser.text: Corning Inc. makes specialized glass, ceramics and optical products that other companies build into networks, screens, vehicles, medicines and solar panels. To understand its business, follow the products it sells, the customers who buy them, and the cash that moves through the factories that make them.

blocks.heading: Where could Corning's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast leaves Corning below today’s $140.91 through October 2028, then reaches only modest upside by October 2029. The weighted prices are $111.11 in October 2027, a 20% loss including dividends, and $129.54 in October 2028, a 7% loss. By October 2029, the weighted price is $139.91, or a 2% return including dividends.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Corning?

paragraphs.text: Operating profit is the main earnings path. The base case rises from $3,465 million to $4,860 million as sales increase from $21 billion to $27 billion and GAAP margins improve from 16.5% to 18%. Optical sales rose 32% in the latest quarter, while Enterprise Networks rose 65%, and Verizon and AT&T announced substantial future demand. The bear case assumes weaker spending and margins, while the bull case requires faster shipments, fuller factories and Solar improvement.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Corning really make?

paragraphs.text: Corning’s own free-cash-flow measure was $1,717 million. It includes realized translated-earnings-contract gains and other cash outside operating activities. An owner may also deduct stock compensation because employees receive shares while existing shareholders absorb dilution. Deducting $286 million leaves $1,127 million. The balance sheet must show whether this cash generation is enough for Corning’s claims.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Corning today?

paragraphs.text: The trailing and forward P/E ratios use different earnings. The first looks backward over the last year; the second uses expected earnings over the next year. A lower forward multiple can therefore mean that profits are expected to recover. Corning’s “core” figures also remove selected items and use constant-currency reporting, which may clarify the trend but can also make earnings look stronger if unusual costs recur.

blocks.heading: How much does Corning pay per share?

paragraphs.text: The dividend stays at $1.12 per share in the base case. That matches the latest $0.28 quarterly declaration and the rate maintained through 2025. The bear case cuts it to $0.84 after the first period as investment absorbs cash. The bull case raises it to $1.20 by the final date, but that requires sustained cash conversion.

blocks.heading: Is Corning’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is the cash left from operations after spending on plants and equipment. Across 2021–25, Corning generated $5,788 million of free cash flow but paid shareholders $7,121 million. In 2025, shareholder payments were $1,162 million against reported free cash flow of $1,413 million. That left only $251 million before other uses of cash.

Corning reduced buybacks over the period, from $781 million to $163 million. Dividends moved in the opposite direction, rising from $871 million to $999 million. Dividends provide a direct cash return; buybacks reduce the number of claims on future earnings. Neither figure alone proves that the company created value.

blocks.heading: What is Corning’s dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: The thin cash yields make future growth central to the valuation. The stock therefore asks investors to believe not only in higher earnings, but in enough recurring cash after factory investment to fund dividends and support the next stage of expansion.

earnings.title: Corning earnings: guidance and what to watch
earnings.meta_description: Corning reports on October 27, 2026; its guidance is clear, but cash generation after capital spending is the key test.
earnings.opening: Corning’s next results are scheduled for October 27, 2026. Watch whether Corning’s growth becomes self-funding after capital spending.
earnings.closing: The full Corning memo also covers Corning’s business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: Management promises a $20 billion annualized sales run rate by year-end 2026. It then targets $30 billion by 2028. The longer-term target is $40 billion by 2030, while its high-confidence targets are lower. For the September 2026 quarter, management guides to core sales of $4,900–$5,000 million. Core EPS guidance is $0.85–$0.89. Capital spending is guided at about $2 billion in 2026.

blocks.heading: Did Corning keep its past promise?

paragraphs.text: Corning also gave shareholders a dated promise. In September 2024, it set a target of 20% core operating margin by the end of 2026. It reached 20.2% in the fourth quarter of 2025, so the company delivered that upgraded profitability target early. That is evidence of execution, but it does not prove that every new manufacturing project will earn an attractive return.

blocks.heading: What do Corning’s last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue reached $4,505 million, up 16.6% from the prior-year quarter. Operating margin improved from roughly 14.8% to 15.5%, while gross margin barely moved from 36.0% to 36.1%. That pattern says more of the improvement came below gross profit than from manufacturing margin alone.

Operating cash flow was $1,717 million, including the $1.0 billion customer advance. Without that advance, operating cash flow was $717 million. Free cash flow was $295 million after capital spending, below the reported figure. The quarter therefore confirms optical improvement, but not a cash rate that can be projected forward.

blocks.heading: What should Corning watch on October 27, 2026?

paragraphs.text: The earnings call is scheduled for October 27, 2026. Investors should check September-quarter results against guidance, the promised improvement in Solar and the pace of capital spending. Reaching the year-end sales run rate would establish a higher starting point for 2027, but sustaining it with stronger cash generation would matter more.
